summary: Cross-reference the inherited 116/69 example to the new faġro communion collocation.
rationale: Keep inherited numbering and text, while exposing the technical noun-bound interpretation in Idiomatic phrases.

summary: Restore the bird as the object of “im Käfig” and correct two typos
before: auf den Tisch gelegt und im Kägif (eingeserrt)
after: auf den Tisch gelegt und den Vogel im Käfig (eingesperrt)
rationale: The supplied translation of 21/34 explicitly distinguishes the apples placed on the table from “den Vogel im Käfig (eingesperrt)”. The entry drops “den Vogel”, making the apples the object of both descriptions. “Kägif” and “eingeserrt” are also evident typos.

summary: Cattle theft is acquisition/removal, not bringing someone out of their mind.
rationale: The Turoyo cattle object and accompanying p.c. gloss exclude sense 2; textual boundary corruption remains a question.

summary: Taking a wife, paying for her, then handing her to another is the marriage frame.
rationale: The entire inherited 26/207 context supports heiraten rather than routine food transport.

summary: Government taking people into military service is not marrying.
rationale: Military destination matches JTM 1.5/4 and the mobilisation passages.

summary: Move the sins/defamation p.c. clause out of marriage.
rationale: The abstract sins object and l ruḥayye cannot illustrate heiraten. Broad taking is a provisional host; full collocational interpretation still needs source confirmation and no new idiom is invented.

summary: 61/250 illustrates traversing a route, now explicit as sense 5.
rationale: Same direct route-object frame recurs at 61/242 and 61/244.

summary: 69/227 seduction belongs to new mental-faculty subsense 2b.
rationale: The full 69/227–228 evidence resolves batch-1 question: removal of judgment from the path and ensuing pregnancy, not merely loss of sanity.

summary: The family obtains a woman for the addressee, rather than themselves marrying.
rationale: Hors 2/19 and bridal allocation at 73/175 jointly support the explicit procurement subsense.

summary: 104/23 illustrates defeating someone at chess, now explicit as sense 7.
rationale: The preceding chess threat and coordinated ġolabwayle resolve the earlier opaque schlagen translation.

summary: File the cattle-taking example under sense 1
rationale: Sense 2 means depriving someone of their reason (məx diḏ-). Both the Turoyo cattle object aq qanyonayḏan and the supplied English “stole all our cattle” describe taking away, covered by sense 1, not loss of reason.

summary: Remove the bringing example from the marriage sense
rationale: The example uses kǝbli/komawbli with an object and a destination l ruḥayye; its supplied translation describes bringing and spreading accusations. It does not concern marriage. Sense 1 already covers taking/bringing, as illustrated by the food-bringing example ybl.III.t.preterit.1. This reclassification does not resolve or alter the figurative English translation.

summary: File taking people into the army under sense 1
rationale: The government takes people into military service (an noše li ʕaskariye; supplied translation “drafts the people into the army”). This belongs to taking/bringing in sense 1, not “heiraten” in sense 3.

summary: New box Infectum-wa: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (Lahdo Traitor 2/29)

data.turoyo: Hiya sti ḥḏo manək d mitawbəlowa lu qaṭlo wa.
data.translation: She also was one of those who were taken to be slaughtered.

rationale: First Detransitive Infectum-wa context; patient is the mother and purpose is killing.

summary: New box ko-Preterit: example for sense 1 in ko-Preterit (MAC MuA The Story of Xalaf Agha/77)

data.turoyo: Ŭ malexu, kombele i+ṗirayḏe!
data.translation: And go, he took his wife!
data.ref: MAC MuA The Story of Xalaf Agha/77

rationale: New ko-Preterit box: kombele parallels narrative mbele and has an overt patient. Analysis is provisional pending recording.

evidence.cite: MAC MuA The Story of Xalaf Agha/77

summary: New box Part act.: example for sense 1 in Part act. (JTM 5.2/34)

data.turoyo: i pire ḥəlla kəle kaṯi, ġaḏ̣ab diḏe, u ġaḏ̣ab diḏe knoḥət larke u zlam, lə mgarela, lə məllale mayko koṯət layko gəzzux, lu mawbəlono du maktub.
data.translation: Die Alte sah ihn kommen, seinen Zorn, seine Wut sah man von Weitem, deshalb sagte sie nichts. Sie fragte den Überbringer des Briefs nicht: Woher kommst du, wohin gehst du?

rationale: First Part act. example: mawbəlono du maktub is a nominal carrier derivative. Final comparison with ḥky III Part. act. maḥkəyone confirms that the glossary includes nominal -ono derivatives in this category; do not require an independent finite predicate.

summary: New box Infectum-wa: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (Talay 2/19)

data.turoyo: Səhḏiwa as sowayḏan, əmmi, i naqqa d me qadišo l qadišo mitawblowa, ya maṭaʕniwayla ʕal ḥaṣe d ḥaywan, d ḥmoro mede, ya arbʕo stene maydiwayla bi darbaste kəmminala, baq qayse, maḥtiwayla ʕal aq qayse ṭəʕniwayla me qadišo l qadišo.
data.translation: Unsere Alten bezeugten und sagten: Wenn die Fangito von einer zur anderen Kirche gebrachte wurde, wurde sie entweder auf den Rücken eines Lasttieres, eines Esels oder so, geladen, oder vier (Männer) trugen sie auf einer Holzkonstruktion von einer zur anderen Kirche.

rationale: Second Detransitive Infectum-wa context, now habitual church-to-church transport; the box was introduced in batch 1.

summary: New sense 4: (mit ʕal) für einen Weg Zeit benötigen, dauern

data.gloss: (mit ʕal) für einen Weg Zeit benötigen, dauern

rationale: LuF 2/4 combines affected travellers aʕlayye with a whole-day duration and a destination, rather than transport of that day. One attestation; internal agreement remains an editorial question.

summary: New sense 1: (Detrans.) weggeholt, fortgebracht werden
rationale: Numbers the previously unnumbered Detransitive meaning attested by the inherited forms and the explicit patient in Lahdo Traitor 2/29.

summary: New sense 5: (mit darbo als Objekt) einen Weg zurücklegen

data.gloss: (mit darbo als Objekt) einen Weg zurücklegen

rationale: The route is traversed rather than transported. Three clauses at 61/242,244,250 confirm the construction; the 61/250 example already exists.

summary: New sense 2b: (mit ʕaql ... m-u darbo) verführen, vom rechten Weg abbringen

data.label: 2b
data.gloss: (mit ʕaql ... m-u darbo) verführen, vom rechten Weg abbringen

rationale: Judgment is taken off the path; pregnancy in 69/228 confirms seduction rather than insanity. Retains a numbered subsense because this mental-faculty pattern is already represented in numbered senses 1 and 2.

summary: New sense 3b: (mit l-) einem Mann eine Frau verschaffen, zur Frau geben

data.label: 3b
data.gloss: (mit l-) einem Mann eine Frau verschaffen, zur Frau geben

rationale: Indefinite plural arrangers assign brides to male partners with l-, distinct from a spouse marrying. This strengthens the procurement reading previously kept under acquisition.

summary: New sense 3b: (mit l- oder ʕal) einem Mann eine Frau verschaffen, zur Frau geben

data.label: 3b
data.gloss: (mit l- oder ʕal) einem Mann eine Frau verschaffen, zur Frau geben

rationale: Indefinite plural arrangers assign brides to male partners with l-, distinct from a spouse marrying. This strengthens the procurement reading previously kept under acquisition. 107/134 adds a clear intermediary with a ʕal-marked nephew as intended spouse.

summary: New sense 6: (mit ruḥ- l-halāk) sich ins Verderben stürzen

data.gloss: (mit ruḥ- l-halāk) sich ins Verderben stürzen

rationale: Reflexive patient and ruin as a result-goal differ from physical transport or loss of sanity. One explicit contextual attestation; same quotation is embedded under ḏym.

summary: New sense 7: (im Spiel) besiegen
rationale: Chess threat at 104/22 and modal 104/23 establish defeating a person, reinforced by coordinated ġolabwayle. Not simply winning/taking material stakes.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (JL 13.12/12)

data.turoyo: i=hawa gməblowa u=tozaṯṯe kule.
data.translation: die Luft nahm seinen ganzen Staub mit.

rationale: Brings the four-example Infectum-wa cell to five and supplies an inanimate causer.

summary: example for sense 3 in Preterit (JTM 3.2/35)

data.turoyo: i ʕaskar di ḥkume w das səwil, mawbəlannene niše
data.translation: die Soldaten der Regierung und die zivilen Soldaten, sie nahmen sie sich zu Frauen.

rationale: First Preterit example for marriage; explicit niše identifies the resulting relation. Suffix segmentation remains open.

summary: example for sense 4 in Infectum (LuF 2/4)

data.turoyo: I qriṯo, d kətyo qaruto, aʕlayye gməblola u yawmo kule, hul d moṭəlla.
data.translation: Um bis zum nächsten Dorf zu gelangen, hätten sie den ganzen Tag gebraucht.

rationale: Sole clear temporal-cost construction; duration, affected travellers and destination are overt.

summary: example for sense 3 in Infectum (LuF 2/37)

data.turoyo: Omər: "Yabo, ono laybi d omannux mede. Gəzzano ṣafro. Haka raḏ̣yo hiya məblolux, alo ono... hat maxlaṣluxli me mede zəd mu qaṭlo."
data.translation: "Mein Lieber, ich kann dir (dazu) nichts sagen. Morgen früh gehen wir hin, und wenn sie einverstanden ist, dich zu heiraten, ich meinerseits... Du hast mich von etwas befreit, das schlimmer ist als Totschlag".

rationale: Thin Infectum marriage cell: a woman is the subject and -lux denotes her prospective husband.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit-wa (MAC Hanna Dewo/218)

data.turoyo: E, ṭabi, əblə́nwanne laṭ+ṭaye, aḏiʕat.
data.translation: Yes, naturally, they brought them to the Muslims, you know.

rationale: Unusual reduced Preterit-wa with plural patients; does not establish marrying by the parents.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (MAC Murder in Kfarze, The Testimony of Farida/37)

data.turoyo: W bəṯr u+lalyo dəqṭilile, midile, blile l ʕIwardo.
data.translation: And after the night in which he killed them, he took them, he brought them to ʕIwardo.
data.ref: MAC Murder in Kfarze, The Testimony of Farida/37

rationale: Unusual m-less blile with a plural patient and explicit destination; representative of the repeated reduced paradigm.

evidence.cite: MAC Murder in Kfarze, The Testimony of Farida/37

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (MAC Murder in Kfarze, The Testimony of Farida/39)

data.turoyo: E. Hedi blole, w bu+lalyayḏa manḥtole li+Qàməšlo.
data.translation: Yes. Then he took her, and on that very night he brought her down to Qamishli.
data.ref: MAC Murder in Kfarze, The Testimony of Farida/39

rationale: Unusual m-less blole contrasts with plural-patient blile in a compact complete transport context.

evidence.cite: MAC Murder in Kfarze, The Testimony of Farida/39

summary: example for sense 3 in Preterit (MAC NE Ditin Hazar/9)

data.turoyo: Mbele a+tlaṯ, mbele a+tlaṯ, ba laṯi mənne, at+tarte rabe, xud i+măsale!? Laṯi mənne saymi ṫə+mede. Mḥalqile li+băṭàlĭye, ŭ kalá háyostene, xud d̥kəmmi, hátuste xud aḥunoni, b̥ṭaʕno, b̥ṭaʕno. L Aloho húlela tre+naʕime, Kguhár zerín,K hawila tre+naʕime, Kguhár zerín.K
data.translation: He took the three (of them), he took the three (of them), couldn’t they do (lit. ‘didn’t it come from them), the two elder (sisters), like they said (lit. ‘like the matter’)!? They weren’t able to do (lit. ‘it didn’t come from them’) anything. He tossed them aside (lit. ‘to their uselessness’), and here’s that one, like they’d say, you’re like my siblings, she is burdened, she is burdened (with a child). God gave her two children, Kgolden earrings,K she had two children, Kgolden earrings.K

rationale: Thin Preterit marriage cell; the wives, elder sisters and pregnancy make the relation recoverable from the full verse.

summary: example for sense 3 in Preterit (MAC NE Farrucke/20)

data.turoyo: Edi mḥawlalle, háwoste mḥawlole, mblole šan ruḥe.
data.translation: Then they moved her, it was that one who moved her, he took her for himself.

rationale: Thin Preterit marriage cell with šan ruḥe and explicit bridal transfer.

summary: example for sense 3 in Preterit (MAC NI Aḥmad Aġa Oṣman Aġa/121)

data.turoyo: Omar, ‘Lawo, qay kəmmat hawxa?’ Aḥmád Aġá koqōmle lu+abro+naʕimo. Omar, ‘Ono komaṇṇux aš+šawʕotayna howina greʕe d Óṣman, w hulíleste i+Səṫṫìyeste, blole. Yabo, šamiʕat’. Omar, ‘Šaməʕno, šaməʕno dəblole, ġamo layt, ʕal u+xēr, šaməʕno dəblole’.
data.translation: He says, ‘Boy, why do you say so?’ Ahmad Agha stands up to his small son. He says, ‘I’m telling you that the seven of us should become Osman’s servants, and I also gave him Səṫṫíye as well, he took her. Daddy, you heard it’. He says, ‘I heard, I heard that he took her, don’t worry, it’s for the best, I heard that he took her’.
data.ref: MAC NI Aḥmad Aġa Oṣman Aġa/121

rationale: Thin Preterit marriage cell: giving Səṫṫiye to Osman and his taking her are presented together; also preserves m-less blole.

evidence.cite: MAC NI Aḥmad Aġa Oṣman Aġa/121

summary: example for sense 3 in Preterit (MAC NI Fingan Agha and Sultan Hasan/2)

data.turoyo: Xalī́l Bag aṯi se Ṣәlṭā́n Ḥasan. Kə́twayle ḥoṯo, húleleyo, i+ḥoṯayḏe, hiwole l Xalī́l Bag. Ḥazna, әšma Ḥáznawa. Hiwole l Xalī́l Bag, hiwole l Xalī́l Bag. Xalī́l Bágstene blole ... i+ḥoṯo ... kogoraš, lo?
data.translation: Halil Bey came over to Sultan Hasan. He had a sister, he gave her to him, his sister, he gave her to Halil Bey. Hazna, her name was Hazna. He gave her to Halil Bey, he gave her to Halil Bey. Halil Bey also took her ... the sister... it’s recording, isn’t it?
data.ref: MAC NI Fingan Agha and Sultan Hasan/2

rationale: Fifth selected Preterit marriage context; repeated giving of the sister to Halil anchors the marriage reading.

evidence.cite: MAC NI Fingan Agha and Sultan Hasan/2

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (MAC NI Fingan Agha and Sultan Hasan/46)

data.turoyo: Omar, ‘Mə‿kəmmutu, blina i+barṯo lo+blìnala? Mək‿kəmmutu?’ Hən mənne əmmi, ‘Mbala!’, ŭ hən mənne əmmi, ‘ʕÁyboyo, náməsyo, ʕáyboyo, náməsyo, lə+blatla.’
data.translation: He says, ‘What do you say, shall we take the daughter, or not? What do you say?’ Some of them say, ‘Take her!’, and some of them say, ‘It’s a shame, she is honorable, it’s a shame, she is honorable, do not take her’.
data.ref: MAC NI Fingan Agha and Sultan Hasan/46

rationale: One context preserves m-less deliberative blina, negative lo+blìnala, and prohibitive lə+blatla together.

evidence.cite: MAC NI Fingan Agha and Sultan Hasan/46

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (MAC NI MAR YUHANEN/8)

data.turoyo: Əmmina, ‘Gəblínanne l Mar Yuḥanǝn’.
data.translation: We say, ‘Let us bring it to Mar Yuhanən’.

rationale: Unusual m-less 1pl Infectum with plural patient and l-goal; representative of the barley sequence.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (MAC NI MAR YUHANEN/12)

data.turoyo: Qām u+Ḥaǧi, u+šuferàyḏanwa, u+Ḥaǧi omar, ‘K_Lawo waki wǝlo ya,_K waki háwxayo, lawo, lǝ+blutǝnne ltamo, ḥētne harke, bi+odaṯe’.
data.translation: The Hajji, he was our driver, the Hajji up and says, ‘Guys, if it is like this, in case the matter is like so, guys, do not take them there, put them here, in this room’.

rationale: Unusual 2pl prohibitive lǝ+blutǝnne with overt goal; contrasted with shorter lǝ+blūtne in the notes.

summary: example for sense 2 in Preterit (PrS 15/2)

data.turoyo: Mawballe ʕaqəl diḏe laǧ ǧən.
data.translation: Die Elfen aber raubten ihm seinen Verstand

rationale: Thin Preterit sense-2 cell; explicit l-agent and ʕaqəl mental-faculty object.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (PrS 28/40)

data.turoyo: Aṯən, laqən bu nxiroyo di kačke. Omər: “Layko gməblatla?” Məlle l abre d Rusṭam lu nxiroyo di kačke, omər: “Gəmmawbannoliyo.” Omər: “Sum kar diḏox” – u nxiroyo di kačke. Mədde l ḥḏoḏe.
data.translation: unterwegs begegneten sie dem Bräutigam des Mädchens, der fragte den Sohn Rustem's: »Wohin führst du sie?« »Nun, ich nehme sie mir mit«. »So mache dich kampfbereit«. Da packten sie einander

rationale: Unusual 1sg + self-beneficiary + patient chain Gəmmawbannoliyo, retained exactly in a clear taking-along exchange.

summary: example for sense 3 in Imperativ (PrS 38/78)

data.turoyo: Aṯən l bə sabʕo, mamṭanne, nayəḥla li kaččəke. Omər: "Awbeloxyo, darwiš, barṯi."
data.translation: dann kehrte letzterer mit dem Löwenfürsten nach dessen Hause zurück. Als sie dem Mädchen die Ohrringe brachten, genas sie. Der Fürst sagte: »Nimm dir meine Tochter mit, Derwisch«,

rationale: Thin Imperativ marriage cell: daughter is explicitly offered to the dervish; reflexive beneficiary -ox.

summary: example for sense 2 in Infectum (PrS 61/107)

data.turoyo: Əmmo: "Gəzzan kurxina ʕal malla d koṯawlan kṯawto d ḥarše, məblina ʕaqəl di kačke d mahəzmo aʕmayna, w gdawṣono u qərran d moyəṯ."
data.translation: "Wir gehen einen Geistlichen suchen, der uns einen Zauberspruch schreibt, dann rauben wir dem Mädchen den Verstand, so dass sie mit uns flieht, und ich beisse den Kaiser, dass er stirbt."

rationale: First Infectum mental-faculty example; ʕaqəl object and intended flight distinguish the use from transport.

summary: example for sense 3 in Imperativ (PrS 63/18)

data.turoyo: Omər: "Haṯe yo, krəḏ̣atla, awbela, lə krəḏ̣atla, ṭraya."
data.translation: "Dies ist sie", erwiderte jener, "willst du sie, so nimm sie; willst du sie nicht, so lass sie."

rationale: Thin Imperativ marriage cell with positive take and negative leave alternatives in the bride proposal.

summary: example for sense 2 in Preterit (PrS 75/58)

data.turoyo: Omər: "Aydarbo", — u taʕlo. Omər: "Warox dayroyo wi. ʕƏbadnowo bi dayro, aṯyo i qaṭun, mawbela ʕaqəl diḏi, əmmo: "Tux, sum aʕmi."
data.translation: "Was ist's denn?" fragte der Fuchs. "Nun, ich bin Mönch gewesen und pflegte im Kloster Gott zu dienen; da kam die Katze und raubte mir den Verstand, indem sie mich aufforderte, bei ihr zu liegen,

rationale: Thin Preterit mental-faculty cell: female agent and ʕaqəl diḏi with the seducing invitation in the same edition sentence.

summary: example for sense 5 in Infectum (61/244)

data.turoyo: Məlle: “Anǧax d doʕanno ʕal i quwayḏi i qamayto w waxtawo, gədmobanno u darbo.”
data.translation: Der Vogel sprach: "Nur, wenn ich meine frühere. Art Wiedergewinne, kann ich den Weg zurücklegen."

rationale: New route-object construction; standalone conditioning on recovered strength. Existing 61/250 is refiled, not duplicated.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (67/9)

data.turoyo: Omər: "ʕAl aʕ ʕayne! Mən ḥreno?" Omər: "Me d maṯno, mbalxulli, qwurxulli, ṯloṯo lalye itux qm i ǧənazayḏi, qm u qawro!"
data.translation: Der Sohn sprach: "Auf die Augen! Was sonst noch?" "Wenn ich gestorben bin und ihr mich fortgebracht und begraben habt, so komm drei Nächte lang zur Totenwache vor meine Leiche, vor mein Grab!"

rationale: Unusual Preterit 2pl agent plus 1sg patient mbalxulli, in an anterior death-and-burial sequence.

summary: example for sense 2b in Preterit (69/228)

data.turoyo: Komər mbele ʕaql di kačke mu darbo. Komər aloho hawxa raḏ̣i, i kačke hawyo l ḥal ḥreno.
data.translation: Er verführte es; Gott gefiel es so: Das Mädchen kam in andere Umstände.

rationale: New seduction subsense; pregnancy in the next clause makes the semantic distinction explicit. Inherited 69/227 is refiled rather than repeated.

summary: example for sense 3b in Infectum (73/175)

data.turoyo: Annaqla aydarbo məblənne? Məblənne i rabṯo lu rabo w d naʕəm w hawxa hul li naʕəmto lu naʕimo.
data.translation: Wie nehmen sie sie nun? Der älteste kriegte die älteste, der nächst jüngere die nächst jüngere, und so weiter bis zur jüngsten; die sollte der jüngste Kriegen.

rationale: New bridal-allocation construction: daughters as patients, l-marked male partners; one verse supplies the whole distributive sequence.

summary: example for sense 3 in Infectum (74/44)

data.turoyo: Gdomər: “Yabo abadan. Ono, i kačkaṯe rḥimoli w žġayni mina mḥaramli a bnoṯe di arʕo ʕal ruḥi, d luyo hiya, lo komobanno bnoṯe.”
data.translation: Er sprach: "Vater, niemals! Ich habe das Mädchen liebgewonnen, und ich habe den Mädchen der ganzen weit außer ihr abgeschworen, und wenn sie es nicht ist, so werde ich keine Mädchen nehmen."

rationale: Fills the still-thin Infectum marriage cell with categorical refusal of other spouses; explicitly contrasts the beloved girl.

summary: example for sense 6 in Preterit (90/111)

data.turoyo: “Aydarbo ono maġraqli ruḥi b i=ḥṭiṯo w mbeli ruḥi l u=halak w ḏəmli u=ḥadodano?
data.translation: "wie konnte ich mich in der Sünde untergehen lassen, mich ins Verderben stürzen und geringschätzig von diesem Schmiede reden!

rationale: New reflexive result-goal construction; the sinner brings himself to ruin, not physically to a place.

summary: example for sense 7 in Infectum (104/22)

data.turoyo: Komər qayəm la tre məštaʕalle, šeṯ naqqat məfqole paṭa. Məlle: “Komannux: hway moro l ruḥux annaqqa, d mawbannux, gqoṭaʕno qarʕux!” Məlle: “Lo naqla howe, ḥamšaḥṣar naqqat howe, aḥ ḥamšaḥṣar naqqat paṭa gnəfqo.” W məštaʕele i naqlayo stene w paṭa məfqole.
data.translation: Da begannen die beiden zu spielen; sechs Mal machte er patt. Der Schah sprach: Ich sage dir: Hüte dich! Wenn ich dich jetzt besiege, schlage ich dir den Kopf ab. - Der Junge sprach: Nicht eine, wenn wir fünfzehn Partien spielen, alle fünfzehn Mal wird patt herauskommen. - Und dann spielte er noch eine Partie und machte auch diesmal patt.

rationale: First Infectum example for defeating a player; explicit game and conditional threat. Existing 104/23 is moved, not duplicated.

summary: example for sense 3b in Infectum (107/134)

data.turoyo: Komər qayəm azzele w mawbele lu kurrək w li səsto w lag gamle w tavda w azzele gab u šex w qrelele. Məlle: “U šex diḏi, tolux, nfaq! Mamṭi li barṯayḏux, mǧaheza mu baytayḏux w mamṭiya, b adyawma ono gmobannola ʕal u braziyayḏux!”
data.translation: Der Sohn machte sich auf, nahm den Jungen mit, samt der Stute und den Kamelen, ging zu dem Scheich und rief ihn: Mein Scheich, komm heraus! Bringe mir deine Tochter und statte sie aus deinem Hause aus! Ich werde sie heute mit eigener Hand mit deinem Neffen vermählen. -

rationale: Thin bridal-procurement cell; intermediary explicitly arranges daughter’s marriage to the addressee’s nephew with ʕal.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit-wa (116/48)

data.turoyo: mbewalle aʕmayye bahro, šroġo
data.translation: ein Licht, eine Laterne, hatten sie mitgenommen

rationale: Thin Preterit-wa sense-1 cell; equipment is anterior to descent. Exact edition fragment is retained without normalization.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (Talay 2/28)

data.turoyo: Annaqqa u mḥasyo du Šamʕən zbiṭ, mawbal lu ḥabs w a ḥrene l aḏiʕi, mdabri u šuġlo, ḥariwo baynaṯṯe w mtasalmi a tarte qəryawoṯe laṭ ṭaye.
data.translation: Nun war aber der selige Šamən gefangengenommen und ins Gefängnis gebracht worden und die anderen haben es nicht verstanden, die Geschäfte zu führen. Sie haben nicht zusammengehalten, und beide Dörfer wurden von den Muslimen eingenommen.

rationale: First complete Detransitive Preterit narrative after two inherited paradigm forms; Šamʕən is patient and prison the goal.

summary: example for sense 3 in Preterit-wa (Jan 1.13/503)

data.turoyo: Koṯe l boli i məštuṯo du Ḥanna d be Ablaḥad, d mawbewole hoṯi i Nəǧo.
data.translation: I remember the wedding of Hanna of the Ablahad family, who had married my sister Nəjo.

rationale: New marriage Preterit-wa cell after round 1; wedding and spouse named.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit-wa (Jan 1.39/1724)

data.turoyo: Ǧan: ʕAmmo Išoʕ əno lo ʕal meqəm kəmšayalno. I naqqa Adnan Mandaras d nafəl w d msəkke, kətwo Demoqraṭ b Məḏyaḏ ste... Kəmmi u ʕAmmo Sḥaqo mawbewolən l Ṣiwas (Sivas) w ġer mene man?
data.translation: Jan: Uncle Isho, I am not asking about before. When Adnan Menderes fell and they arrested him, there were Democrats in Midyat too ... You say they had taken Uncle Sḥaqo to Sivas. Who else besides him?

rationale: Transport Preterit-wa has three examples after round 1; explicit fronted patient and Sivas goal add a complete interview context.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infinitiv (Jan 1.35/1431)

data.turoyo: Əno mu tuwbilo w mu ṭəmtiyayḏe lə kʕuǧazno, bale mu nəmnəmayḏe du darbo.
data.translation: I am not bothered by taking him there and bringing him back, but by his mumbling on the road.

rationale: Traditional Detransitive Infinitiv box contains only tubilo/tawbilo forms; this supplies a connected action-noun context, without claiming patient-subject syntax.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (Jan 3.56/1630)

data.turoyo: W kəḏʕi hanək di qaflayo komitawbəli lu nḥoro, bu darbo ste kobodən bu rʕoyo.
data.translation: And those of that group know that they are being taken to slaughter; even on the way they begin grazing.

rationale: Thin Detransitive Infectum cell: plural animal patients and slaughter goal explicit.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (Jan 3.56/1630)

data.turoyo: W hanək, d fayiši taḥt iḏoṯe du ruʕyo ste, kəḏʕi, d aḥ ḥawronaṯṯe lu nḥoro mtawbəli.
data.translation: And those who remain under the shepherd's hands know that their companions have been taken to slaughter.

rationale: Detransitive Preterit has three examples after round 1; contrasts completed removal with preceding komitawbəli.

summary: Move “Sergey and” from the Turoyo field to the English translation
before: Lu Sargey w li Gule aq qanyonayḏan kulle blǝnne/mballe. ‘’Sergey and
after: Lu Sargey w li Gule aq qanyonayḏan kulle blǝnne/mballe.

data.translation: Sergey and Gule stole all our cattle.

rationale: The raw example contains the complete English sentence “Sergey and Gule stole all our cattle.” Its beginning and stray quotation marks were left in the Turoyo field, while the translation field starts mid-sentence. Restore the two fields together.

summary: Restore the missing “zu” in “kommen zu können”
before: mit sich um zu ihrem Vater kommen können
after: mit sich, um zu ihrem Vater kommen zu können
rationale: The German purpose clause requires the infinitive “kommen zu können”. This corrects the entry’s grammar without changing its interpretation of ḥatta d-oṯən.

summary: Correct “hicht” to “nicht”
rationale: “hicht” is a typo for “nicht”. The source translation has “hören nicht”, and lo=ko-šəmʕi supplies the negation.

summary: Restore “das” before “ganze Vieh”
rationale: The neuter singular collective “Vieh” requires “das ganze Vieh” here; the supplied translation of 75/232 contains this article and the Turoyo has u=ṭarš kule.

summary: Sense 1: revise the gloss
before: a) wegholen, mitnehmen; b) dörfliche Formen: wegholen, mitnehmen; c) nehmen;
after: a) wegholen, mitnehmen, (hin)bringen; b) dörfliche Formen: wegholen, mitnehmen, (hin)bringen; c) nehmen;
rationale: Explicit l-goals and transported objects demonstrate bringing as well as removal; this clarifies directionality, already implicit in inherited food-bringing examples.

summary: Sense 2: revise the gloss
before: j-n um den Verstand bringen (məx diḏ-);
after: j-n um den Verstand bringen (məx diḏ-, ʕaqəl diḏ-);
rationale: PrS 15/2 has ʕaqəl diḏe as the affected mental faculty; meaning is unchanged but the attested noun alternative is added.

summary: New idiom: mawbele/mawbəl ʕəmro (ʕumro) 'sein Leben verbringen'

data.turoyo: Mbelan ʕəmran bu+məqamawo, hul uʕdo.
data.translation: We have spent our life in this way until now.

rationale: Repeated lifetime-object construction at Famine/30,59 and interview 1/3,4. Searches for ʕəmr and ʕumr found no existing ybl collocation.

summary: New idiom: mawbele/mawbəl w mamṭele/mamṭe ḥḏoḏe 'im Kampf hin und her agieren'

data.headword: mawbele/mawbəl w mamṭele/mamṭe ḥḏoḏe 'im Kampf hin und her agieren'
data.turoyo: mawballe w manṭalle ḥḏoḏe, w mawballe w manṭalle ḥḏoḏe
data.translation: der Kampf zwischen ihnen wogte hin und her, hin und her.

rationale: Paired combat collocation rather than a meaning of ybl alone; searches for mawballe w and manṭalle found none. The exact contribution of each verb remains open.

summary: New idiom: mawbele/mawbəl xabro, bəšra (mit l-) 'eine Nachricht, eine Freudenbotschaft bringen'

data.headword: mawbele/mawbəl xabro, bəšra (mit l-) 'eine Nachricht, eine Freudenbotschaft bringen'
data.turoyo: Azze mḥalqile bu baḥar. Mawballe u xabro lu Saʕid, əmmi: "Hawilox tre qaṭune." Omər: "Ḥalequnne, heš u nošo d lo šaməʕ."
data.translation: Der Diener ging und warf sie in's Meer. Dem Said aber brachten jene die Nachricht: "Es sind dir zwei junge Katzen geboren worden." "Ersäuft sie!" befahl er, "bis jetzt hat es noch keiner vernommen." Man warf sie in's Wasser.

rationale: Message noun is the object and l- marks recipient. PrS 43/111 adds bəšra. The existing hyw 1 xabro idiom uses a different verb.

summary: New idiom: mawbele/mawbəl foṯo 'sich aufmachen, eine Richtung einschlagen'

data.headword: mawbele/mawbəl foṯo 'sich aufmachen, eine Richtung einschlagen'
data.turoyo: Bəṯr ma tmonaḥṣar əšne qayimi m tamo w səmme raḥil, rawixi ʕal ag gamlaṯṯe w mawbele u ṭaršawo, d kətwo, w mawbele foṯe yalla! D əzze lu bayto, d aṯi mene meqəm.
data.translation: Nach achtzehn Jahren brachen sie von dort auf und zogen weiter. Sie bestiegen ihre Kamele, nahmen das Vieh, das vorhanden war, mit, und er machte sich auf nach dem Heim, von dem er früher gekommen war.

rationale: The face is not literally transported; destination is the following homeward clause. Existing hyw/mḥy face expressions use other verbs. One attestation.

summary: New idiom: mawbele/mawbəl zor d- 'die Oberhand über jemanden gewinnen'

data.headword: mawbele/mawbəl zor d- 'die Oberhand über jemanden gewinnen'
data.turoyo: Li kačke ḥəlla, d u zlamano u sowo mbele zor d Badran, mḥelele ḏ̣arbo du mawto.
data.translation: Das Mädchen sah, daß der alte Mann die Oberhand über Badran bekam und ihm einen tödlichen Schlag versetzte.

rationale: zor is the nominal component; victory and mortal blow establish the interpretation. Exact mbele zor search found no prior entry. One attestation; d- relation remains open.

summary: New idiom: mawbele/mawbəl ṭabiʕa 'eine Natur, eine Eigenschaft annehmen'

data.headword: mawbele/mawbəl ṭabiʕa 'eine Natur, eine Eigenschaft annehmen'
data.turoyo: Aḏəʕ, ənnu u səsyano mbele i ṭabiʕa daq qanyone, i naqla d moyaṣwa mi turto.
data.translation: Der Mann hatte also erkannt, daß das Pferd die Natur der Rinder angenommen hatte, als es an einer Kuh saugte.

rationale: Abstract trait-taking with a horse acquiring cattle nature; noun search found the verse embedded under myṣ but no existing ybl idiom. Keep the noun-bound use outside the numbered sense list.

summary: New idiom: mawbele/mawbəl w mamṭele/mamṭe ḥḏoḏe 'einander im Kampf hin und her reißen, den Kampf hin und her führen'

data.headword: mawbele/mawbəl w mamṭele/mamṭe ḥḏoḏe 'einander im Kampf hin und her reißen, den Kampf hin und her führen'
data.turoyo: mawballe w manṭalle ḥḏoḏe, w mawballe w manṭalle ḥḏoḏe
data.translation: der Kampf zwischen ihnen wogte hin und her, hin und her.

rationale: Paired combat collocation rather than a meaning of ybl alone; searches for mawballe w and manṭalle found none. The exact contribution of each verb remains open. 95/119 supplies a literal wrestling counterpart to the earlier spear-fighting context. Retain one example.

summary: New idiom: mawbele/mawbəl zor, zoriya d- 'die Oberhand über jemanden gewinnen, jemanden niederzwingen'

data.headword: mawbele/mawbəl zor, zoriya d- 'die Oberhand über jemanden gewinnen, jemanden niederzwingen'
data.turoyo: Li kačke ḥəlla, d u zlamano u sowo mbele zor d Badran, mḥelele ḏ̣arbo du mawto.
data.translation: Das Mädchen sah, daß der alte Mann die Oberhand über Badran bekam und ihm einen tödlichen Schlag versetzte.

rationale: zor is the nominal component; victory and mortal blow establish the interpretation. Exact mbele zor search found no prior entry. One attestation; d- relation remains open. Repeated strength-object uses in 96/276,277,284 and 111/85,90 confirm the meaning; d- marks the opponent as possessor of strength.

summary: New idiom: mawbele/mawbəl xṭuṭo 'eine Furche ziehen'

data.turoyo: A ṭlawḥe w ak kušne, hawxa bu šəklano kozərʕənne: u daworo komobəl xṭuṭo w kowe ḥa bəṯre, kobozər a ṭlawḥe aw ak kušne bəṯre, yaʕni kobozarre b gawe du xṭuṭo.
data.translation: Linsen und Wicken werden auf folgende Weise gesät: Der Landmann Ackert eine Furche, und einer geht hinter ihm her und streut die Linsen oder die Wicken hinter ihm aus, das heißt, er streut sie in die Furche hinein.

rationale: Technical furrow-making collocation, not transport of an existing furrow; xṭuṭ search found no prior listing. One attestation.

summary: New idiom: mawbele/mawbəl faġro (mit mən-, m-iḏe) 'den Leib des Herrn empfangen, die Kommunion empfangen'

data.headword: mawbele/mawbəl faġro (mit mən-, m-iḏe) 'den Leib des Herrn empfangen, die Kommunion empfangen'
data.turoyo: Azze Šamʕən, mbele faġro w daʕər. Daʕər, yatu.
data.translation: Schamun ging, empfing den Leib des Herrn, ging zurück und setzte sich.

rationale: Six occurrences establish the sacramental noun collocation. Existing 116/69 under sense 1 is cross-referenced rather than repeated; faġro search found no ybl idiom.

summary: New idiom: mawbele/mawbəl laḥmo ʕam ḥḏoḏe 'miteinander auskommen'

data.turoyo: Haṯe hiyya w i Fərdo lə kməbli u laḥmo ʕam ḥḏoḏe Alo, zaḥme yo.
data.translation: She and Firdo will not bring bread together. By God, it is difficult.

rationale: New bread-harmony collocation; no matching headword in laḥmo ʕam search. Machine English remains literal.

summary: New idiom: mawbele/mawbəl mede l-u rišo 'etwas zu Ende bringen'

data.headword: mawbele/mawbəl mede l-u rišo 'etwas zu Ende bringen'
data.turoyo: U Sḥaqo zlam fahəm we ġalabe, bas mu sabab d kətwe agoist, huwwe w u aḥuno, lə qədriwo məbliwo mede lu rišo ʕam ḥḏoḏe.
data.translation: Ishaq was a very understanding man, but because he was selfish, he and his brother could not bring anything to completion together.

rationale: New completion collocation, reciprocal cooperation context; lu rišo lookup had no match.

summary: Routine counts supplied with this batch: III Preterit 1=584, Infectum 1=349, Imperativ 1=99, Infectum-wa 1=34, Infectum 3=16, Preterit 3=4, Preterit-wa 1=1. These are evidence counts, not existing-example counts or additional decision rows; do not sum repeated counts across batches.

Valency: transported objects can be bare NPs, topicalized NPs resumed by suffixes, or suffixes alone; overt l-agents occur in Preterit beside l-goals/recipients, so l- cannot be assigned one role without checking the clause.

Aspect: -wa covers habitual transport and hypothetical/past prospective contexts. JL 16.7/18 has bare Preterit in an anterior clause under a future main clause; the verb box is not a tense translation.
Detransitive mitawbəlowa (Lahdo Traitor 2/29) presents the mother as transported patient, suppressing the agent, with lu qaṭlo purpose. No new function beyond being taken away is forced.

Reduced mb-, məbl-, bl- and əbl- coexist with mawbl-; select a few complete, distinctive examples rather than every repeated contraction. Do not infer a new root from reduction. The read-only entry mbl lookup returned no entry; retain the inherited cross-reference and ask about its target.

The already listed bīr idiom extends from noticing to remembering: JTM 5.2/37 has failed recall and MAC NE Samson the hero/18 has a neglected action expressed by a d-clause. No new numbered motion sense is warranted.
JL 11.12/9 and MAC NE Shangali Pangali/13 pair taking with bringing back. Translation of the pair as swaying/sharpening does not independently establish either sense for ybl.

Final category check: ḥky III labels nominal maḥkəyone as Part. act. Therefore the agent noun mawbəlono at JTM 5.2/34 is included under the required Part act. label, with its nominal syntax stated. This supersedes the initial decision to withhold a box merely because the token was a noun.
Batch 2 continued from all three predecessor files before selection. No routine_counts are supplied in this batch; prior routine totals are not counted again.

New evidence resolves two earlier questions: 69/227–228 establishes seduction as 2b, and 73/175 supports third-party bridal procurement as 3b. This supersedes the batch-1 classification of Hors 2/19 gməblinaluxyo under acquisition 1; earlier occurrence rows remain as an audit trail. Existing 26/207 has already been moved to spouse-subject marriage 3.
The inherited 61/250 route example is moved to 5. LuF 2/4 temporal cost remains 4, distinct from traversing a route whose object is darbo.

A bride moved to a groom by unspecified plural escorts (PrS 87/1) is still transport 1. Self-benefit alone does not prove marrying; distinguish actual spouse-subject marriage, bridal allocation and physical transfer.

The piž proposal at 61/242 remains uncertain: “Haymen uʕdo lo kəmbanno piž bu darbo d mobanne.” The edition reads “Wahrlich, jetzt kann ich den Weg nicht wiederfinden und zurücklegen.” This combines two verbs; it cannot prove a separate ybl find sense.

No automatic citation repair: PrS text/verse references and inherited prs page/line references can denote the same passage (e.g. mawbálle-le muklo); differing conventions do not demonstrate an erroneous citation.
Batch 3 retains all earlier labels. Defeat at chess is 7 and ruin as reflexive result-goal is 6. Winning the actual knucklebones at 115/35 remains 1 because the Turoyo does not specify fair winning.

Strength-taking and the paired combat expression converge across texts; earlier single-attestation wording is now supported by 96/276–284, 111/85–90 and 95/119. These are shared collocations, not fresh senses for each text.

Detransitive contrasts: past-habitual transportation of a church object at Talay 2/19 versus patient-oriented completed imprisonment at Talay 2/28. The reader’s new_form flag for -wa is obsolete after batch 1, not evidence of an additional box.

The ʕal-marked nephew in 107/134 belongs to marriage procurement 3b. The intermediary subject does not himself marry the girl. The room-goal in 95/57 remains physical transport even with an adjacent marrying predicate.

Communion is a noun-bound technical collocation of faġro with an optional priest source, supported by 116/63,64,67,68,69,77; retain only one new idiom example and the inherited 116/69 cross-reference.
The question concerning 104/23 schlagen is resolved by chess and ġolabwayle. The earlier draft question remains only insofar as the unrelated p.c. sins text still requires clarification.
Jan Beṯ-Şawoce has no edition translation. Supplied English is project machine translation, retained verbatim where quoted; semantic decisions rest on the Turoyo.
Read final round-1 batch ybl~b3, retaining its labels through 7 and subsenses 2b/3b. No new numbered senses and no duplicated round-1 proposals are needed here.
Full mawbl- coexists with reduced mbl-/bl-/b- and split m beliwo spellings. New examples are selected after accounting for round-1 additions, not the readers’ stale cell totals.

The glossary convention puts tuwbilo under Detransitive Infinitiv; its syntax here denotes Isa taking someone, not necessarily being taken. Preserve the inherited form category and distinguish semantic argument roles.
The paired animal passage contrasts komitawbəli, ongoing removal, with mtawbəli, completed removal. Slaughter goal does not itself create a new verbal sense.
Lə mawballe at Jan 2.15/3483 is a doubtful memory formula with no bir/bolo. Do not silently turn this into a new ybl memory idiom; root, segmentation and experiencer coding need verification.
Read-only lookups laḥmo ʕam and lu rišo found no existing matching collocations; mawballe and bir searches were also checked. Round-1 zor and inherited bīr were inspected before deciding duplication.
Resolve the inherited → mbl cross-reference: no entry mbl was returned by the supplied lookup.
Confirm gməblola in LuF 2/4: agreement, status of u yawmo kule, and aʕlayye. The temporal-cost construction is accepted from one contextual attestation, without imposing a speculative segmentation.
Confirm kombele in MAC MuA The Story of Xalaf Agha/77 as ko-Preterit rather than reduced Infectum.
Check school lo+kәblәnne/gəblənne (MAC Hanna Dewo/57–58) and bele (MAC NE Story of Joseph/4) against the recording; root identification is unresolved.
Check məblile (JL 15.6/10), mawbele (JTM 3.3/5), speech repair məblila/mbela (MAC NE Unfortunate Youth/14), and gender-looking Mbeeela (MAC NE ezo koviye/5); no uncertain example added.
Confirm suffixes in məblinallene, mawbəlannene, mbánnanne, mbálunxuyo and the m-less blutu/blutǝnne/blūtne sequence. No unverified person segmentation is published as a paradigm.
Is mobəl bīr retrospectively remember an ordinary range of merken, or should the existing idiom gloss be widened? No duplicate idiom created.
Does inherited 69/227 ʕaqəl ... m-u=darbo denote seduction rather than loss of sanity? Preserve its wording and ask before moving it to sense 2.

Inherited ybl.III.t.infectum.13 is provisionally refiled under broad taking 1, away from marriage; confirm its sins/defamation collocational interpretation before assigning a new idiom. Inherited ybl.III.t.infectum-wa.1 (104/23) needs source checking because schlagen is not transparent transport.

The p.c. cattle example has an English fragment in its Turoyo field and a truncated translation. Confirm the source text rather than reconstructing it. Also resolve inherited translator-check notes and the Russian editorial question under sense 3.
PrS 1/16 lacks the cow-taking clause in its supplied German; no example or replacement translation is added. PrS 18/24 needs water/boat agent and agreement confirmation.
Confirm the productive status of mawbəlono du maktub. It is now provisionally included in Part act. following the glossary’s nominal -ono practice; the exact derivation is still open.
Check kubilane (PrS 22/2) segmentation before extracting a new paradigm; provisions and recipient do not transparently match the suffix analysis.
Confirm syncretic məblənne/məblile boxes at PrS 33/3, 41/121, 72/28,75 and 75/28–30; narrative order or German anterior tense cannot alone decide the box.
Confirm who leads whom at PrS 40/11 and 26/179; the edition’s recasting and the Turoyo l-marking require independent checking.
Confirm piž in 61/242, the individual role of rišo at 67/67, and d- after zor at 64/163; no separate trace-finding or head-running meaning has been established.
Confirm suffix/person readings of gməblalle (64/154), mballa (73/438), mballe (73/455), obeləlle (64/175), and the self-benefit endings in mawbanni/mobanni.
Is the ṭabiʕa collocation productive for other acquired traits? The current evidence is one horse/cattle-nature passage, also quoted under myṣ.
Inherited ybl.III.t.infectum.13 is provisionally refiled under broad taking 1, away from marriage; confirm its sins/defamation collocational interpretation before assigning a new idiom.

Confirm final -e in gmawbele (95/252), gender/agent suffixes in məblola (96/323, 98/56), final -yo in məbloliyo (96/352), and final -ne in mballalluxne (Talay 1/275). Retain textual variation, do not normalize it from the edition translation.

Check lə mawballe at Jan 2.15/3483: omitted memory noun, a different lexeme, or transcription? No secure experiencer pattern can be inferred.

summary: Obtaining a woman for another person (Hors 2/19) and taking people into military service remain acquisition/transport, distinct from the subject marrying a spouse. The translation erben at Hors 2/152 does not independently establish inheritance.
ʕaqəl and məx are alternative mental-faculty objects; seduction with m-u=darbo at inherited 69/227 may be a related but narrower collocation; do not equate it automatically with loss of sanity.

Taking people into military service remains acquisition/transport. The translation erben at Hors 2/152 does not establish inheritance. Third-party bridal procurement from Hors 2/19 is reassigned to 3b after the explicit allocation evidence at 73/175, superseding the batch-1 note.
Abstract honour removal can accompany literal daughter removal; namus can metonymically denote the woman. Hyperbolic weight loss through fright also retains deprivation. No additional numbered sense.
Vehicles and waves extend the transporter role to inanimate causers, continuing batch 1.

Horn movement by blows, flood-water carrying and divine retrieval of life as entrusted property extend transport/removal without new senses. Honour/woman metonymy is repeated; no independent new marriage sense.
The round-1 strength-taking zor/zoriya idiom recurs with collective Syriac strength, opposing enemies and deaths; no repeated proposal.
Existing bīr memory idiom recurs as kmawbələd bir; the voiced -əd ending is preserved and queried, not normalized.
buneno-l-ox-ne is highly reduced presentation in recollection; male speaker Išoʕ does not support reader 1sg.f. The clause remains a first-person presentation extension.
Hail removes/destroys the grain crop, continuing round-1 weather/wind causer extensions.
Household goods have l-marked human recipients; ownership transfer versus safekeeping is not resolved by the Turoyo alone.
Institutional seat/theme transferred to Damascus extends the transported theme, with its referent recovered from discourse.
Wedding party transporting the bride is physical III.1, not spouse-subject marriage III.3.
Military destination and purpose denote transport to service; round 1 already moved inherited drafting example out of marriage.
